body:
## Summary

The chat timeline's tail-scroll controller enters an **unbounded self-referential layout loop**. `LayoutUpdated` calls `StartBringItemIntoView`, which itself causes a layout pass, which re-raises `LayoutUpdated`. The only brake is a version check that is not invalidated while the chat view stays loaded, so the UI thread spins forever and the app becomes fully unresponsive.

This is **not** a slow-render or heavy-load issue. A single qualifying event is enough.

- Windows reports `AppHangB1` (stopped interacting with Windows)
- UI thread at **71.2s CPU** while every other thread stayed under 6s
- Working set grew **230 MB -> 999.9 MB** during the hang
- Reproduced on a freshly restarted process within ~27 minutes of uptime

## Affected build / environment

| | |
|---|---|
| App | OpenClaw Companion (`OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI.exe`) `2026.9.4.0` |
| OS | Windows 11 25H2, build `26200.9550` |
| Runtime | .NET 10.0.12, win-x64, self-contained |

## Root cause

`src/OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI/Chat/ReactorItemsViewScrollController.cs`

### The loop closes

```csharp
// line 181
private void OnLayoutUpdated(object? sender, object args)
{
    DetachLayout();
    ...
    itemsView.DispatcherQueue.TryEnqueue(() =>
    {
        if (_disposed || !_valid || !itemsView.IsLoaded || version != _version
            || itemsView.ScrollView is not { IsLoaded: true })
        {
            if (!_disposed && _valid)
                AwaitLayout();          // re-arms LayoutUpdated
            return;
        }

        AttachScrollView();
        if (!StartTailRequest(request) && !_disposed && _valid)   // line 205
            AwaitLayout();                                        // never reached, see below
    });
}

// line 254
private bool StartTailRequest(TailNavigationRequest request)
{
    ...
    _following = true;
    itemsView.StartBringItemIntoView(request.Index, new BringIntoViewOptions   // line 269
    {
        AnimationDesired = false,
        VerticalAlignmentRatio = 1.0,
    });
    return true;      // line 274 -- always true on the success path
}
```

1. `LayoutUpdated` fires.
2. `StartTailRequest` calls `StartBringItemIntoView` (line 269).
3. `BringIntoView` **itself triggers a layout pass**, re-raising `LayoutUpdated`.
4. Goto 1. Repeat.

`StartTailRequest` returns `true` whenever it gets past the guards, so the `AwaitLayout()` fallback at line 205 is unreachable on that path. The only exit is the `version != _version` check at line 196, and `_version` is only incremented in `OnUnloaded` (line 282). **While the chat view remains loaded, that exit never triggers.**

Every iteration allocates a fresh `BringIntoViewOptions`, which is what drives the 4x memory growth.

## Stack trace (symbolized from a live dump)

Captured with `procdump -ma` on the hung process and resolved with `dotnet-dump` against the PDBs shipped alongside the binary. This is the actual stack at hang time, not inference.

```
OS Thread Id: 0x58d4
  ABI.Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.IItemsViewMethods.StartBringItemIntoView(
      WinRT.IObjectReference, Int32, Microsoft.UI.Xaml.BringIntoViewOptions)
      index = 0x0000000000000060        (96)
  Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.ItemsView.StartBringItemIntoView(Int32, BringIntoViewOptions)
  OpenClawTray.Chat.<...InitialTailPositioner>.StartTailRequest(TailNavigationRequest)
      [...\src\OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI\Chat\ReactorItemsViewScrollController.cs @ 269]
  OpenClawTray.Chat.<...InitialTailPositioner>+<>c__DisplayClass20_0.<OnLayoutUpdated>b__0()
      [...\src\OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI\Chat\ReactorItemsViewScrollController.cs @ 205]
  ABI.Microsoft.UI.Dispatching.DispatcherQueueHandler.Do_Abi_Invoke(IntPtr)   <-- UI thread
  Microsoft.WinUI!ABI.Microsoft.UI.Xaml.IApplicationStaticsMethods.Start(...)
  OpenClawTray.Program.Main(System.String[])
```

Full dump available on request (1011 MB, PID 16712).

## Trigger in practice

Any burst of layout changes in the chat timeline. The most common source is the gateway broadcasting `sessions.changed`, which rebuilds the session and chat lists. Three events inside a single millisecond immediately preceded this hang:

```
15:36:07.162  [INFO] [EVENT] Received event: sessions.changed
15:36:07.163  [INFO] [EVENT] sessions.changed received - refreshing sessions list
15:36:07.164  [INFO] [EVENT] Received event: sessions.changed
15:36:07.165  [INFO] [EVENT] sessions.changed received - refreshing sessions list
15:36:07.165  [INFO] [EVENT] Received event: sessions.changed
15:36:07.165  [INFO] [EVENT] sessions.changed received - refreshing sessions list
```

Process state at capture: `Responding=False`, 54 threads, 999.9 MB, UI thread 71.2s CPU.

## Suggested direction

Not a prescribed patch, just the constraints a fix needs to satisfy:

1. **Stop re-entering on the layout caused by our own scroll.** Track whether a `BringIntoView` is in flight and ignore `LayoutUpdated` until it completes, instead of relying on a version counter that only changes on unload.
2. **Make the guard at line 196 actually reachable**, or remove it if it is not load-bearing. Today `StartTailRequest`'s unconditional `true` makes the `AwaitLayout()` branch at line 205 dead code.
3. **Bound the retry.** `AwaitLayout()` re-arming on every failed attempt is the other half of the loop. A cap or a coalescing queue would bound it even if the scroll path is wrong.
4. The project already references `System.Threading.Channels`, and the existing `_tailNavigationQueue` / `QueueTailRequest` path (line 230) looks like the intended coalescing point. Worth checking whether the `LayoutUpdated` path (line 194) bypasses it.

## Impact

Any user running an agent that emits tool calls while the chat window is open. The process must be killed; the session data survives but the UI is unusable until restart. Recovering UI resources also requires a restart (see #1567 for the leaked popup windows).

## Required proof pools

- `UI` (chat)

## Real behavior proof

Hung-process dump plus the symbolized UI-thread stack above, captured from the shipped `2026.9.4.0` binary using its own PDBs.

## Validation

Report, not a code change. Stack trace produced from a live dump of the hung process.

## Additional reproduction on 2026.9.4 (startup / restored chat)

I reproduced what appears to be the same native-chat UI-thread failure on the current installed Windows Companion, with a healthy local Gateway.

### Environment

- Windows 11 Pro `10.0.26200`, x64
- Companion `2026.9.4+3c43751b2bace876de3febe478ebabeca172e3ac`
- Gateway `2026.9.8 (fc23bc8)`, loopback `ws://127.0.0.1:18789`
- 41 existing sessions; `models.list` returned 21 models

### Observed sequence

1. Companion had started in tray mode and connected to the Gateway, but no visible window appeared. The process reported `Responding=True` with `MainWindowHandle=0`; enumerating its top-level windows showed `OpenClaw Chat` existed but was `Visible=False`.
2. Repeated `openclaw://chat` activations were received and logged (`Handling deep link`) but did not make the existing chat window visible.
3. After terminating that instance and cold-starting the executable with `openclaw://chat`, a real main window was created (`MainWindowTitle=OpenClaw Companion`, nonzero handle).
4. Once the operator connection completed and the native chat restored state/catalog data, the window became permanently unresponsive. Gateway health/tick traffic continued normally. The process reached about 65 seconds of CPU and ~257 MB working set within roughly two minutes.
5. A cold start with `openclaw://commandcenter` remained responsive (`Responding=True`, ~2 seconds CPU), isolating the problem to the chat surface rather than general startup, pairing, or Gateway connectivity.

The relevant log boundary was:

```text
[ChatBridge] OnModelsListUpdated: count=21
Wizard response payload kind=Object len=27626
Node status: Connected
```

There was no matching Gateway failure; `openclaw health --json` returned `ok: true` with all 20 plugins loaded and no plugin errors.

### A/B workaround confirmation

Changing only this setting and restarting with `openclaw://chat` recovered the app:

```json
"UseLegacyWebChat": true
```

After 22 seconds the same Companion was connected, visibly open, and responsive (`Responding=True`, ~3.8 seconds CPU, nonzero main-window handle). No sessions, credentials, or Gateway settings were changed.

This corroborates the native timeline/tail-positioning path as the failure boundary. It also explains why ordinary monitoring can misdiagnose the initial state: `Responding=True` is not meaningful when `MainWindowHandle=0`.

I did not attach a full dump because it may contain session/auth data. I can collect a redacted current-process stack if maintainers need confirmation against `InitialTailPositioner.StartTailRequest -> ItemsView.StartBringItemIntoView`.

## Reproduction on Windows Companion 2026.9.8.0

Hit the same UI hang in 2026.9.8 (the build running on my machine today) with the Application Hang 1002 trace below. Posting here to confirm the fix is still needed against the latest release, not just 2026.9.4.

### Environment

- Windows 11 (eDMateXPro, Tailscale-attached)
- Companion 2026.9.8.0 (`OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI.exe`)
- Mac mini Gateway 2026.9.4 (loopback via Tailscale)

### Application Hang events (Event Viewer)

| Time               | PID    | Event | Source            |
|--------------------|--------|-------|-------------------|
| 2026-10-08 18:39:31 | 29764 | 1002  | Application Hang |
| 2026-10-08 17:23:13 | 18316 | 1002  | Application Hang |
| 2026-10-03 23:10:55 | 15076 | 1002  | Application Hang |
| 2026-10-02 00:26:55 | 18048 | 1002  | Application Hang |

The 18:39:31 entry is the moment the chat window went "not responding" in the title bar. The hang reproduces on 9.8, not just 9.4.

### Companion tray log, around 18:39:31

```text
[18:39:14] session.message
[18:39:15] chat (chat.history request, final user prompt)
[18:39:16] agent run_status / assistant stream
[18:39:18] agent stream=item
[18:39:19] chat history response (100940 B)
[18:39:19] assistant final 726 B
[18:39:19] ActivityStream notification
(no further log lines after this — UI thread deadlocked)
```

The 18:39:19 line is the last entry before Application Hang 1002 fired at 18:39:31 (~12 s later, consistent with the 5 s "not responding" threshold plus OS retry). Network/receive threads kept logging until the OS killed the process — matches the tail-scroll controller loop described in the issue body.

### Workaround

```powershell
Stop-Process -Name "OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI" -Force
```

Process has to be relaunched from the Start Menu; it cannot recover on its own.

Happy to capture a `procdump -ma` on the next hang if that helps.

Still reproduces on **2026.9.8-1** against Gateway **2026.10.5** (Windows 11).

Hang dump (ProcDump `-h`, 23 Oct 2026): the UI thread is blocked in `Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.ItemsView.StartBringItemIntoView`, called from `ReactorItemsViewScrollController` → `InitialTailPositioner.StartTailRequest`, dispatched via `DispatcherQueueHandler`. Windows logs `AppHangB1`.

The code path is unchanged on `main` (f5978f0).

Coalescing `sessions.changed` refreshes (see #1569) made the hang rarer but did not stop it.

Can share the managed stack on request.

## Reproduction on 2026.9.8.0 (deterministic at every launch) + evidence that the re-arm loop is not the only problem

**Environment**: Windows 11, Companion `2026.9.8-1` (file version `2026.9.8.0`), Gateway `2026.10.6`, managed local gateway, **native** chat (`UseLegacyWebChat=false`), no SSH tunnel.

**Symptom**: every launch hangs within ~2 s of the node handshake completing. The window is created and visible (1280x860, `Visible=True`), but `Responding=False`. Windows logs `AppHangB1`: 5 events — 2026-10-27 19:04, 2026-10-28 09:44, 09:45, 09:49, 11:05. At 90 s wall the UI thread had burned **101 s CPU** (~100% of one core) while every other thread stayed flat; the log keeps writing from background threads (gateway health, node ticks), so this is UI-thread-only.

**Managed stack** (`dotnet-dump collect --type Full`, SOS `clrstack -all`):

```
Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.ItemsView.StartBringItemIntoView(...)
  ABI.Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.IItemsViewMethods.StartBringItemIntoView
  OpenClawTray.Chat.<ReactorItemsViewScrollController>...__InitialTailPositioner.StartTailRequest
      Chat/ReactorItemsViewScrollController.cs @ 269
  <>c__DisplayClass20_0.<OnLayoutUpdated>b__0        @ 205
  ABI.Microsoft.UI.Dispatching.DispatcherQueueHandler.Do_Abi_Invoke
  Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Application.Start -> OpenClawTray.Program.Main
```

### New data point: does `StartBringItemIntoView` return?

The review asked for this. I patched `InitialTailPositioner.OnLayoutUpdated` to run **at most 8 times** (a guard on the re-arm path, leaving `StartTailRequest` untouched), shipped it and restarted: **the UI thread still sat at 97% and the window stayed unresponsive.**

So the managed `LayoutUpdated` -> re-arm loop alone does not explain the hang: a single `StartBringItemIntoView` invocation does not return (or returns only once XAML aborts the layout cycle). That is worth knowing before choosing a repair — a fix that only debounces/limits the re-arm will not help.

### Mitigations I verified on the shipped binary (no source change)

| Change | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `UseLegacyWebChat: true` | App usable, legacy web chat surface |
| `StartTailRequest` body -> `return false;` (never call `StartBringItemIntoView`) | Starts fine, `Responding=True`, idle CPU ~0%, no AppHang. Cost: no auto-scroll to newest message |
| `StartTailRequest` body -> `ScrollView.ScrollTo(0, ScrollableHeight)` | Unblocks, but raises `LayoutCycleException` (caught by the app's unhandled-exception handler; chat pane sometimes renders blank), so I would not ship it |

A source-level fix should probably stop using `StartBringItemIntoView` for tail positioning entirely (or defer it until the item container is realized and bounded), rather than trying to make the loop converge.

I can share the full dump (705 MB), the exact IL patch, or the AppHang event export if useful.

Additional live reproduction on **OpenClaw Companion 2026.9.8-1**, installed source revision `2ba89f377ce8ce3f5ddfc452e4d509329f109114`.

### Observed behavior

- Windows repeatedly reports the client as not responding.
- The process consumes approximately 98-100% of one logical CPU core.
- Three independently collected live managed stacks stop at the same UI-thread call:

```text
ABI.Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.IItemsViewMethods.StartBringItemIntoView(...)
Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.ItemsView.StartBringItemIntoView(...)
OpenClawTray.Chat.InitialTailPositioner.StartTailRequest(...)
OpenClawTray.Chat.InitialTailPositioner.<OnLayoutUpdated>b__0()
ABI.Microsoft.UI.Dispatching.DispatcherQueueHandler.Do_Abi_Invoke(...)
Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Application.Start(...)
OpenClawTray.Program.Main(...)
```

Compiler-generated type names are shortened here. No application memory dump, chat content, credentials, or raw protocol logs are attached.

The Gateway remains healthy independently of the frozen UI: `/healthz` returns HTTP 200 with `status=live`, and `/readyz` returns HTTP 200 with `ready=true`, `coreReady=true`, and `eventLoop.degraded=false`. Requests from both Windows and the WSL Gateway environment complete in approximately 4-11 ms. The client's existing Gateway connections remain established.

### Source cross-check and remaining uncertainty

The installed revision calls `StartBringItemIntoView` synchronously from the UI dispatcher in `ReactorItemsViewScrollController.cs:269`. This matches the captured stacks directly.

However, the explanation of a simple `LayoutUpdated -> scroll -> LayoutUpdated` application-event loop needs qualification:

- `OnLayoutUpdated` calls `DetachLayout()` before enqueueing the scroll callback.
- `Request()` also increments `_version`, not only `OnUnloaded()`.
- `TailNavigationPolicy.CanExecute` already checks the queued target's bounds and identity.

The live stacks establish the blocked scroll path, but do not by themselves prove an application-handler recursion or an invalid index. A native WinUI layout/navigation problem, or an unsafe interaction between tail positioning and layout state, still needs to be distinguished with an isolated reproduction.

I am investigating the client repository and a focused regression/fix. No fix is claimed or validated yet.

Fix proposed in **#1935**: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/pull/1935

The native production-root regression reproduces the UI-thread hang inside synchronous `ItemsView.StartBringItemIntoView` when navigating past a tall, virtualized assistant message. This is a Windows chat scrolling defect, not a Gateway responsiveness failure. The evidence does not establish a managed `LayoutUpdated` recursion.

The fix uses low-priority dispatch and asynchronous native-element bring-into-view, preserves exact native target geometry and anchor lifetime, and rebinds an unfinished request when Reactor recycles its target container. Existing tail-generation checks, lifecycle cleanup, and the user's scroll-up position remain intact.

Validation for commit `b98c89bcee5249177c4dc564064f4828a0ae7425`:

- Full production build passed.
- Shared: **4,807 passed**, 25 existing skips; Tray: **4,763 passed**, no skips.
- Selected native regression/lifecycle/root checks: **19 passed**, no skips.
- Five tail-regression cases passed again in a fresh process, then **five passed after rebuilding the clean committed head**.
- The native cases cover narrow/wide history, append, remount, preserving scroll-up, and an explicit history-revision jump.
- GPT-6 Astra **Standards** review: no significant issues. **Spec** review: no significant issues.

Proof boundaries: native execution used the currently installed WinUI runtime (`Microsoft.UI.Xaml.dll` 3.3.0.0). This does not claim validation against the original installed client's 3.2 runtime, a live Gateway/provider replay, or the complete `windows-winui-interactive` maintainer pool. The original installed client and its profile were not replaced, restarted, or modified.

Additional answers to the review's native-navigation questions and the corroborating reports above:

**Deterministic trigger:** the minimized native regression is now in [PR #1935 (fix(chat): chat freezes when opening tall message history)](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/pull/1935), in [`HistoryTail_ScrollsPastTallMessageWithoutBlockingUi`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/blob/b98c89bcee5249177c4dc564064f4828a0ae7425/tests/OpenClaw.Tray.UITests/ReactorChatLayoutProofTests.cs#L1232-L1361). It uses 16 synthetic mixed-role messages: index 5 has 50 paragraphs of 40 CJK characters plus a 10-row table; the newest row is separated from that tall row and initially unrealized. Thus the reproducer does not require sharing a user's conversation or full dump. The pinned development base is `4cbbe51c45a7653e75ecf7d85481d7014b7e374b`, not a claim that today's upstream main was freshly reproduced.

**Return versus re-arm:** in the baseline native reproduction, UI-thread progress stopped at the synchronous `ItemsView.StartBringItemIntoView` boundary and an external watchdog was required. Together with the repeated released-process stack samples, this supports treating a blocked synchronous navigation call as the repair boundary. It does **not** prove an unconditional managed `LayoutUpdated` recursion or a particular internal WinUI defect. A debounce/re-arm cap alone cannot make an already-blocked native call yield, consistent with the earlier eight-entry-cap report.

**Why not just scroll to `ScrollableHeight` or disable positioning:** disabling navigation drops the tail-follow behavior. Using the current estimated total extent is not proof that the unrealized last item's actual bounds are visible, and the reported layout-cycle result makes that unsuitable as a demonstrated replacement. The PR instead uses asynchronous native target geometry, completion/anchor ownership and rebinding when an unfinished target is recycled.

**Dump requests / responsiveness:** the sanitized stack and synthetic reproducer are sufficient for this regression; I am not requesting anyone's full memory dump, which can contain conversation and authentication data. As Bcobas noted, `Responding=True` without a visible chat window is not acceptance evidence. The follow-up therefore inspected the actual full-process window and the final text marker's bounds, not only the process flag.

**Honest current status:** the full-app fixture now demonstrates initial 240-message tail visibility, streamed append follow and session reselection on the PR head, using a synthetic Gateway and isolated profile. However, Notifications > Back still clipped the streamed final answer, and reader scroll-up retention has not been demonstrated in the full app. The exact 16-message trigger is still native-root test-host proof only. The PR's Real Behavior Proof records these gaps; this issue should not be considered verified fixed or ready to close from those partial results. A visible out-of-process recovery launcher is not implemented by this focused fix.

title: Chat tail-scroll controller spins the UI thread at 100% CPU on layout changes
